concepts.title: Personal wardrobe interview
concepts.premise: An appealing wearer introduces a look, then gives its objects personal meaning. Curiosity about a person sustains the sequence.
concepts.script: Source architecture: identity/place → item questions → personal provenance → complete outfit/accessories → playful human close. Prepare questions and preserve actual answers. New ad copy and any sales handoff follow the current copy SOP and evidence rules.
concepts.fixed: One recognizable wearer; questions motivate attention; memory stays with the speaker; whole outfit resolves the details.
concepts.variable: Number of items, location, interview length, caption treatment and an explicitly added target CTA. The personal story must be authentic or transparently dramatized.

concepts.assets: One authorized wearer/look and question/answer source; full silhouette and face coverage; distinct detail views only for selected items; caption transcript if used; optional verified target CTA.
concepts.calibration: R01 is 45.21s with three framing segments. Direct changes at f670/22.333s and f1202/40.067s bracket a wider outfit section. Serif phrase captions change without creating picture cuts. No separate B-roll or sales end card was observed.

edit.coverage: One full-frame wearer. Keep face, garment and microphone clear; no permanent split-screen. Detail coverage is usually a motivated in-shot reframe.
edit.cuts: Cut at a question/topic reset, a needed scale change or the closing reaction. Preserve complete memory, foot/bag gesture and joke response. No periodic punch-in timer.
edit.transitions: Direct cuts, zero overlap. A continuous tilt/approach is camera movement, not a dissolve. No default wipes or flashes; any target brand fade is a separate optional ending event.
edit.broll: Default separate B-roll is zero. If an item cannot be read in the primary frame, insert its actual detail on the named item, hold through orientation, and return to the same answer/face after recognition. Keep interview audio continuous.
edit.motion: Move medium → wider for garment; follow the wearer’s reveal; settle before a small detail needs reading. Avoid post zoom during the emotional answer. Proposed crop changes depend on source resolution, not guessed reference keyframes.
edit.text: Optional restrained serif phrase captions over a low-detail torso region; generally one or two lines. Move the caption region when it would cover the named item. Replace with actual phrases, independently of picture cuts.
edit.audio: Prioritize question/answer and useful ambient continuity. Preserve thoughtful pauses and laughter. Any music stays subordinate; no fabricated sentimental SFX during personal history. Exact source mix is unverified.
edit.finish: Natural skin/material color and coherent daylight; match exposures between real takes. No routine speed changes, freezes, fake handheld shake or aggressive glamour filter.
edit.ending: Return to the face for the final human response. A target offer/tag is an explicit addition, with readable hold and verified facts; do not overwrite the actual answer.
edit.adapt: Shorten by selecting fewer complete item modules, not clipping the meaningful memory. Lengthen through specific follow-ups and new details, not extra crops. Protect approved words and reaction time.
edit.reject: Reject invented provenance, covered emotional answers, unreadable accessories, false brand authentication and repeated detail footage. Check exact answer meaning and caption sync.

concepts.fixed: Meaningfully different wearers/looks; full look before close detail; actual item movement follows questions; return to person before switching encounters.
concepts.variable: Participant count, event setting, encounter length, detail order and optional captions. A brief answer may remain brief.

concepts.calibration: R11 is 114.87s with seven women, nine continuous visual segments and eight cuts at f179,707,1094,1799,1855,2360,2462,2746. Six cuts introduce wearers and two jump within encounters. Most item changes happen through camera movement. No added captions.

edit.coverage: One wearer fills the frame at a time. Establish full silhouette, then follow actual accessories and return to face. Do not treat each downward tilt as another shot.
edit.cuts: New wearer at resolved answer/thanks; within-encounter jump only for a useful detail or redundancy. Preserve different encounter lengths; no mandatory per-person shot count.
edit.transitions: Direct hard cuts, zero overlap. Weather/background changes may remain if they mark a new encounter. Avoid dissolving two faces together or adding a wipe for each item.
edit.broll: Default zero separate B-roll. A needed insert must show that wearer’s actual item at its question cue, preserve the answering audio and return before the next personal question. No generic brand stock under provenance.
edit.motion: Follow extended hand, turning bag, raised foot or exposed earring. Settle long enough to inspect. Return upward intentionally; do not whip between unrelated body parts or manufacture digital shake.
edit.text: Source uses no added captions. Target captions are an explicit accessibility/delivery choice: short accurate phrases with moving safe placement away from the item. Item labels need verified names; omit uncertain labels.
edit.audio: Keep enthusiastic but intelligible questions, answers and event ambience. Smooth discontinuous room tone only where needed. Optional music supports energy without covering a quiet respondent.
edit.finish: Preserve real event texture and diverse light; correct exposure/color for readability without erasing the environment. No routine slow motion or speed ramps over speech.
edit.ending: Allow the final wearer’s reply/smile to resolve. A brand handoff is an explicit target adaptation, never a claim the reference participants endorse that product.
edit.adapt: Shorten by fewer distinct encounters or fewer questions; lengthen through new looks and meaningful answers. Never make seven speakers recite the same benefit to fill time.
edit.reject: Reject near-identical looks passed off as diversity, wrong accessory at a cue, clipped answers and invented brand names. Check all camera reveals and each encounter’s completion.

concepts.premise: Host and guest reveal taste and personality through a shared cultural interest; their relationship is the main visual subject.
concepts.script: Accessible recommendation questions → specific anecdotes/banter → more personal belief or experience → shared close. Prepare a question ladder; preserve actual answer meaning. The source is not a direct product VSL.
concepts.fixed: Speaker/listener relationship, topic chapters and meaningful two-shot holds. Expressions can be more useful than literal pictures of named places.
concepts.variable: Topics, number of chapters, locations, participants and a separately justified brand ending.
beats: Both people answer/react within an immediately readable shared setting.
Primary two-shot; opening question → initial answer or joke lands.
3–8s module; cut for an actual answer/reaction.
Both faces establish a relationship, not a presenter monologue.
Guest gives concrete detail; alternate closer guest and two-shot by meaning.
Primary speaker; answer begins → detail complete → return shared frame.
2–6s views; longer complete thought may hold.
Closer face concentrates information while wider return preserves rapport.
Cut to host/listener when the reaction adds meaning.

New position/background with both speakers recognizable.

Location/color change marks a chapter while wardrobe anchors continuity.
Hold two-shot or speaker/meaningful listener through complete anecdote.
Primary conversation; personal turn → story and response resolve.
Longer shared attention gives emotional weight and pace contrast.
Two-shot → optional guest reply close → shared finish.
The social exchange resolves without an unearned sales interruption.
styles: T

Primary conversation and topic orientation.
F
Closer face/listener coverage from compatible eyeline and setting; no invented camera provenance.
Information emphasis, performed quotation, listening and reaction.
concepts.assets: Authorized speakers and actual/staged dialogue; two-shot plus meaningful faces; chapter locations; accurate transcript/topic labels. External B-roll only for a demonstrated information gap.
concepts.calibration: R07 runs 133.07s. Topic/location changes occur at f400,1430,2068,2524,2971,3851. A 9.83s two-shot spans f3196–3491. At f3671 the guest is shown listening while the host continues. No literal restaurant/shop B-roll or sales end card.

edit.coverage: Two-shot is the relational anchor; guest/host/listener faces are primary conversational coverage, not generic B-roll. Keep consistent eyelines and readable hands/mics.
edit.cuts: Cut on informative emphasis, a new answer, a revealing response or a chapter. Preserve the reaction after humor and the full emotional thought. No alternating close/wide pattern merely to hit a timer.
edit.transitions: Direct cuts and restrained reframing. Location chapter changes can be hard cuts with continuous conversational context. Proposed J/L cuts require actual audio alignment; they are not certified source settings.
edit.broll: Default external inserts are zero. Add one only if a necessary detail cannot be understood from speech/gestures; enter on that referent, leave before the relational punchline and return to speaker/listener. Do not automatically cover named restaurants.
edit.motion: Walking scenes may track backward while keeping both faces legible. A discrete crop can emphasize a speaker; hold the new scale rather than bounce each sentence. Keep text fixed in frame during any post transform.
edit.text: Separate persistent topic title from phrase captions. Proposed vertical layout: topic near upper clear space, speech in lower middle above interface exclusion. Change the title only at chapter cues; preserve short complete phrases.
edit.audio: Conversation, laughter and pauses lead. Bridge ambient discontinuities without implying continuous location when it changed. Optional music stays under both voices; maintain natural listener timing.
edit.finish: Natural street/editorial color and consistent skin tone; wardrobe supplies palette. No unsupported slow-motion or freeze treatment over a real response.
edit.ending: Resolve the shared thought and goodbye. A target brand tag is separate from the conversation and must not create fictitious endorsement.
edit.adapt: Shorten by fewer chapters while keeping question/answer/reaction. Lengthen by deeper anecdotes and meaningful follow-ups, not more crop changes. Protect the personal section’s slower pace.
edit.reject: Reject stock food covering a joke, reaction shots that reverse meaning, fabricated spontaneity and topic labels that overstate expertise. Verify actual speakers/captions and timing.

concepts.title: Greenscreen comparison and service guide
concepts.premise: A visible guide earns attention through concrete comparisons, then explains a method/service and shows the action destination.
concepts.script: Rapid paired examples → guide identity/promise → distinct selection criteria → process/interface → desired outcome and destination. Verify prices, criteria and credentials; AI or recorded presenter is a target production choice.
concepts.fixed: Stable guide; predictable comparison layout; different diagrams for different concepts; intentional switch to interface demonstration.
concepts.variable: Number/categories of comparisons, criterion count, graphics layout, service and CTA. Reduce examples before making prices unreadable.

Overlay above stable presenter; first name → first item, second name → second item.

Simultaneous objects let viewers inspect the contrast.

1.8–3s per additional pair; 2–6 pairs total including G1 if useful.
New examples build breadth without new layout learning.
Clear product clutter and let face explain the promise.

Distinct body, palette, contrast or styling card for the named idea.
Overlay at its criterion → leave/replace before next criterion; avoid face.
1.2–3s per simple card; longer for actual reading.
Each graphic answers a different question; a reused generic chart would blur meaning.
Small presenter cutout over readable actual interface area.

concepts.assets: Approved presenter; two accurate cutouts per comparison; verified comparison facts; distinct criterion graphics; actual destination/interface; transcript and mask-safe compositions.
concepts.calibration: R05 is 28.91s. Six paired examples occupy 0–11.07s; presenter/criteria follow; keyed website section is 19.93–23.47s; profile CTA is 25.60–26.87s. Overlay changes and base presenter resets are separate events.

edit.coverage: Presenter is base; product/diagram cards are overlays, then interface becomes background with smaller keyed presenter. Keep the mouth/eyes visible and the active evidence area unobstructed.
edit.cuts: Change comparisons on each new pair, not each caption word. Clear overlays for persona/interpretation. Reset body footage at a clean phrase seam; hidden cuts beneath cards remain separate from card events.
edit.transitions: Direct base cuts. Proposed graphic entrances: 0.15–0.30s short slide or scale from the assigned side, then settle; do not animate prices while reading. Remove outgoing pair before unrelated one overlaps. Interface handoff is one layout event, not a chain of wipes.
edit.broll: Product and criterion assets annotate the guide rather than cover the whole screen by default. Website coverage begins on process language and ends when the guide interprets the benefit. Each insert needs a named exit and return state.
edit.motion: Keep camera stable. Direct guide gesture toward the active evidence region. Scroll only enough to show the relevant function; avoid uncontrolled full-page movement. Inspect mask edges, glasses and hand occlusion.
edit.text: Separate comparison labels/prices, criterion names, speech captions and CTA arrow. Proposed safe layout reserves face/mouth zone and a lower caption band; adjust for actual aspect/subject. Verify all numbers and labels.
edit.audio: Brisk rhythmic pair naming can ease into explanatory speech. Keep voice continuous through graphics; optional soft comparison accents only where they clarify a change. Align after final voice, not model timestamps.
edit.finish: Consistent room light and clean edges. Match asset scale for fair visual comparison, not misleading real-size equivalence. No speed-ramped presenter speech; interface movement can be edited only without misrepresenting function.
edit.ending: Use actual current destination and one clear action. Circle/arrow starts when named and leaves enough unobstructed reading time. Optional benefit line returns to presenter after the destination is understood.
edit.adapt: Shorten by fewer pairs/criteria, not sub-readable prices. Lengthen with meaningful worked examples or actual process actions. Resolve dense diagram time conflicts before generation.
edit.reject: Reject face-covering products, stale prices, false identical-quality claims, duplicated criterion graphics, illegible scrolling and fake credentialed personas. Check every layer independently.

concepts.title: Podcast-style reverse-selling listicle
concepts.premise: A stable speaker frames desirable benefits as ironic reasons to avoid the product; changing illustrations make the argument concrete.
concepts.script: Provocative exclusion/hook → distinct numbered reasons → interpretation/product introduction → sensory or use detail → verified value/offer. The target copy SOP still governs new argument development; irony cannot invent proof or invert real risks misleadingly.
concepts.fixed: One speaker anchor, distinct propositions, full-speaker rhetorical resets, semantically timed lower-panel inserts and a deliberate product reveal.
concepts.variable: Reason count, duration, reveal point, panel proportion and types of evidence. Microphone styling does not establish a real independent podcast.
beats: Speaker plus an immediately legible product/outcome illustration.
Split layout; hook referent → turn introducing first reason.
3–6s hook module; cut to full speaker on numbered reset.
A visual promise makes the rhetorical inversion understandable.
Full speaker delivers reason title or sarcastic turn.
Remove lower insert at reason opening → restore only when a concrete illustration is named.
Expression carries the joke and organizes the list.
Distinct action, sensory metaphor or substantiated explanatory view.

concepts.assets: Stable presenter performance; distinct beat-linked inserts; approved product views; supported claim/offer ledger; accurate captions; final aligned narration. No reference adoption/stock statistics transfer automatically.
concepts.calibration: R02 is 112.64s. Full-speaker resets include f131,369,666,1006,1436,1672,1751,2029,2706; a product close emphasis occurs at f2050/82s. Upper speaker/lower illustrations and seam-area captions dominate. Generator and podcast provenance are unknown.

edit.coverage: Proposed vertical split starts near half frame, adjustable for face and evidence. Full speaker is a separate state, not merely an empty lower panel. Keep captions near a stable seam/clear region without obscuring product or mouth.
edit.cuts: Enter a reason on speaker, cut the lower panel on semantic action change, return on qualification or punchline. Do not cut the upper speaker whenever lower footage changes. Preserve ironic pauses and complete demonstrations.
edit.transitions: Zero-overlap cuts between lower-panel inserts and for rhetorical resets. Proposed product punch is one discrete closer framing at introduction, held through recognition. No continuous zoom bounce or mandatory wipes. Any overlap belongs only to a justified within-insert process.
edit.broll: Enter on the clause it explains, not at the top of an unrelated sentence. Leave before price/policy/interpretation unless the image directly serves it. Return to P at every reason transition where expression matters. Metaphor, actual demonstration and evidentiary footage each have explicit status.
edit.motion: Stable speaker; varied meaningful action inside inserts. A macro may move slowly to expose texture; explanatory animation follows the actual causal interaction. Avoid repeating generic reactions or a single science view.
edit.text: Short uppercase phrase captions in a consistent high-contrast treatment are an available source-matched direction. Keep reason numbers as structural text, claims/offer as verified labels, captions as exact speech. Separate their event timing.
edit.audio: Voice anchors all visual changes; direct dry delivery with intelligible pauses for irony. Music subordinate; minimal accents at a real rhetorical turn. Do not invent audio cuts from the visual edit; align real final voice first.
edit.finish: Presenter world remains consistent; insert media may differ deliberately by semantic job. Normalize readability without making documentary-like clips into glossy product film. No unapproved narration speed changes.
edit.ending: Reveal timing follows the brief, not source percentage. Finish with visible exact product and truthful offer/action. Generic romantic imagery cannot support a guarantee or customer count.
edit.adapt: Shorten by fewer supported reasons or simpler illustrations within authorized copy scope. Lengthen via new proof or explanation, not more filler panels. Preserve each proposition’s speaker → illustration → interpretation logic.
edit.reject: Reject fictitious expert/customer endorsement, repeated source clips, unsupported molecular proof, irony that reverses factual meaning and pictures that lag their clause. Verify every insert exit/return.

concepts.script: Visual sequence rather than spoken VSL: material/action → construction variation → finished form → worn/carry confidence → brand. Sparse chapter copy may carry the thought; do not invent documentary manufacturing claims.
concepts.fixed: Distinct visible actions, tactile scale, purposeful macro-to-whole progression, slower ownership payoff and readable identity finish.
concepts.variable: Product-specific operations, number of details, color variants, sparse text, optional recorded material sound and end-card duration.

concepts.calibration: R03 has 12 segments/11 direct cuts in 17.43s at 4:5. Process shots run about 0.53–1.80s; carry f300–410 holds 3.67s; brand f410–523 holds 3.77s. Three restrained text chapters, no spoken sales argument.

edit.coverage: Full-frame details and wider payoff; no presenter or inset architecture required. Image hierarchy changes from contact/action to complete object to wearer.
edit.cuts: Cut when a new operation, scale or ownership phase adds information. Complete the visible function even if a musical tick arrives early. Lengthen the payoff after quicker construction details.
edit.transitions: Direct cuts, zero overlap, are the base grammar. Match direction or contact when useful but do not fake continuous manufacture across different products. Optional final fade is target direction, not observed source necessity.
edit.broll: The film is primary visual storytelling; process/details can serve as B-roll in a larger hybrid only at a matching craft/function cue. In that case exit after action completion and return to the parent speaker or whole product, not an unrelated stock scene.
edit.motion: Subject/tool action leads. Controlled following movement can track carry; a macro camera move is justified only if it reveals a surface or part. Avoid automatically pushing into every still.
edit.text: Sparse chapter copy, consistent clear zone and modest scale. Give each phrase enough uninterrupted time; one chapter may span several shots. Logo is a separate ending event.
edit.audio: Plan atmospheric/original music and selected tactile contact/closure/footstep sounds when appropriate. Use actual sound or transparently designed effects; exact source effects were not verified. No obligatory voice track.
edit.finish: Warm materials, controlled neutrals and coherent contrast. Preserve actual material color. No unverified speed ramps; slow footage only when authorized and physically convincing. Avoid heavy grain masking product detail.
edit.ending: Whole/carry recognition precedes brand. CTA is optional to the target brief and cannot replace the entire ownership payoff.
edit.adapt: Shorten by fewer distinct operations while preserving whole product and carry. Lengthen through meaningful craft/use details, not longer logo padding or repeats. Do not imply a process the brand cannot substantiate.
edit.reject: Reject misrepresented workshop provenance, impossible tool contact, changing hardware/material, cropped silhouette and identical actions in different files. Verify that styling remains the main desired outcome.

edit.coverage: Full-frame causal action. Use two-shot for request, closer action for consequence, wider reveal and reaction framing. Covering details remain in the same animated world.

edit.motion: Use eyelines and physical reveal before extra effects. Track both characters for request, widen for hidden context, settle for recognition. Camera must not expose the secret prematurely.
edit.text: Default no editorial captions. Diegetic phone/sign content must remain legible if it carries the joke. Optional brand tag is separate; do not use explanatory paragraphs to rescue unclear staging.
edit.audio: Design original action accents and music around request, consequence, reveal and reaction. A pause or held sound can protect anticipation. Source no-speech finding is model-assisted; exact source sound timing is not certified.
edit.finish: Consistent stylized materials, character age/body, wardrobe and prop size. No accidental morphing as transition; no unnecessary speed ramps that shorten the readable action.
edit.ending: Resolve the twist and reaction before optional CTA. A loop may reconnect desire only if understandable; do not crop away the punchline to make it loop.
edit.adapt: Shorten by a simpler premise/fewer causal steps, not by removing recognition. Lengthen only for added meaningful action or reaction. Test silent comprehension before adding audio.
edit.reject: Reject age/wardrobe drift, wrong carried prop, extra limbs, incorrect door geography, unreadable phone, premature reveal and incomplete reaction. Inspect every transition frame.

edit.cuts: One direct cut for each new actual item. Preserve count-to-item agreement and stable recognition. Do not add a second pose cut within a sub-second item hold.

edit.audio: Optional count provides progression; align final number onset to item change. Music supports momentum. Check intelligibility and real beat alignment; source model estimates are not edit markers.
edit.finish: Match exposure/background and honest color. Do not resize products into false physical equivalence. No speed manipulation that makes products unreadable; stills can hold unchanged.
edit.ending: Finish the last count and item. CTA or loop is a target choice; a full-set return should be deliberate, not a second repeated catalogue cycle.
edit.adapt: Total roughly equals intro plus N recognition holds plus optional ending. If over duration, reduce item count only within brief scope or simplify labels; do not silently omit promised items.
edit.reject: Reject wrong count, duplicated models, unsubstantiated ranking, hidden handles, unreadable labels and mismatched spoken numbers. Compare real silhouettes, not filenames.

concepts.calibration: R13 is 17.32s. First cycle starts f0,9,17,27,35,45,53,63,71,81 and restarts f89; holds about 0.27–0.33s. Ten recurring compositions repeat. No spoken script/captions/CTA card observed. Actual capture method unknown.

edit.coverage: Full-frame still images of one product. No presenter layer or mandatory explanatory text. The rapid sequence itself supplies motion impression.
edit.cuts: Direct replacement on deliberate rhythm with recognition checks. Alternate whole, signature and construction scale rather than adjacent near-identical crops. Return whole after a detail cluster.
edit.transitions: Zero-overlap hard cuts. No morphs, simulated product transformation or automatic crossfades. Loop handoff is a planned visual return only if authorized by the brief, not repeated multi-cycle filler.
edit.broll: These are primary visual product views; in a narrated hybrid insert a relevant detail only on its descriptor, leave after recognition and return to the parent product/speaker state. Do not reuse this rapid rhythm for complex mechanisms.
edit.motion: No within-still motion required. A new physical angle adds information; digital crop/zoom does not establish a new scene. If a real action is needed, change the asset plan rather than pretending still replacement demonstrates it.
edit.text: Default no captions. Any feature name/price must receive real reading time and exact evidence. A three-tenths-second slot is unsuitable for an offer paragraph.
edit.audio: Music may guide image rhythm; listen to actual track and choose cut accents. No assumed source BPM or exact synchronization. Optional subtle effects must not overwhelm tactile recognition.
edit.finish: Consistent neutral backdrop, material hue, grain/finish and hardware. Light may emphasize different surfaces while product identity stays fixed. No unnecessary speed manipulation of stills.
edit.ending: Resolve into full silhouette before optional identity/action. A single purposeful sequence is preferred under visual-variety rules; a loop needs a clear brief-specific role.
edit.adapt: Shorten by selecting fewer distinct features while keeping whole/detail/whole comprehension. Lengthen by genuinely new physical views or a different useful action, not repeat cycles. Complex construction gets longer holds.
edit.reject: Reject invented compartments/hardware, inconsistent strap attachment, falsely certified material/scale, duplicated source crops and rapid abstract flashes that obscure the object. Verify every still against approved product references.

concepts.title: AI UGC greenscreen product story
concepts.premise: One conversational creator remains as a small keyed guide while changing background images make a product argument visible. This family combines the Nuamore-style visual language with documented Eleanor travel and Vivienne quiet-luxury revisions. Its continuity comes from the guide and narration; its variety comes from genuinely distinct backgrounds, actions and viewing scales.
concepts.script: Choose discovery, styling adviser or opinion/reframe mode in the family skill. For new copy apply Hook → Problem → Brief problem → Agitation → Solution/category → Dismissal → UMP → UMS → Solution intro → Future pacing using supported social proof, with the current SOP and evidence limits. Fashion emphasizes an attractive outfit and useful selection criteria; unsupported mechanisms or testimony are never invented. Preserve exact approved narration. The slots below are visual jobs: merge, repeat or move them only to follow the authorized script. An approved styling guide may identify its product before the examples; an opinion ad may show the product from frame one and name it later. Record visible reveal and spoken reveal independently.
concepts.fixed: One deliberate guide identity and voice; separate editable picture/presenter/caption/audio tracks; background changes tied to meaning or action; imagery shows the specific styling/detail being discussed; varied B-roll with controlled product identity; aspiration before utility in fashion; current truthful destination/offer.
concepts.variable: Single-action versus optional grid hook; early versus delayed target appearance; phone-like versus more polished natural fashion coverage; presenter corner/size; intentional presenter exit for a readable close; number of looks and duration of each; still/motion mix; optional detail crop; product-and-action or authentic page ending. Voice/provider/casting are resolved from the actual brief, not copied automatically from W01.
beats: Hook: establish immediate desire or a compelling styling proposition
A wearer already stepping with a striking complete look, or a legible grid of genuinely distinct approved style examples. Keep a clean region for the guide.
First frame with opening phrase. Leave when the proposition is understood and the next thought changes the viewing job. A delayed-reveal grid excludes the target until its designated cue.
Proposed 2–5s per opening visual; an approved longer hook may need additional distinct evidence rather than a static overfilled grid. Direct background cut; guide/voice continue.

The viewer can see the desired look immediately, making the spoken hook concrete. A grid signals range only when each outfit/product remains readable; action impact comes from desirability, not unrelated distress.
Problem/brief problem/agitation: make the fashion tension recognizable
A distinct dressing or outfit scene showing the relevant decision: a cuff adjustment, a knit beside jeans, or an actual authorized style comparison.
Enter on the specific familiar tension; stay through the visible action. Advance on the category alternative or guiding criterion, keeping the same narrator.
Proposed 2–5s per distinct action; protect the gesture and readable silhouette. Direct cut.
The tension stays connected to getting dressed and expressing taste. It does not turn an aspirational argument into exaggerated failure imagery or imply a fabricated customer history.
Solution category and dismissal: show the route and the remaining gap
A new considered wardrobe arrangement or dressing detail that illustrates the category choice while the guide explains its limitation.
Enter when the alternative becomes specific; exit on the phrase introducing better selection criteria. Omit as a separate picture if the approved short script combines these thoughts.
Proposed 2–5s; can share one useful continuous picture with the adjacent thought. No compulsory extra shot at a sentence boundary.
A concrete wardrobe example lets the viewer understand what is being considered. The creator supplies the interpretation; the image is not presented as proof that every alternative fails.
UMP to UMS: explain the relevant selection logic
A precise shape, texture or material relationship visible at the scale the line needs; compare silhouette to an outfit only when the copy calls for it.
Enter on the exact criterion such as shape or texture. Hold through the relationship, not merely the noun. Move to product introduction when the spoken logic reaches it.
Proposed 2–4s per independently useful view; extend for comprehension. Direct scale change; optional background-only step crop if the source has detail.
The visual makes an ordinary fashion criterion inspectable. Do not invent a hidden scientific cause or use one generic macro for every claimed quality.
An unobstructed whole-product view, or a deliberate hand touch showing the same selected item and color.
Enter on the exact product-name cue; this slot may move earlier for an approved styling guide. The target may already have appeared if its visual reveal is unrestricted.
Proposed 2–4s including enough recognition time. Direct cut, with stable guide and continuous voice.
A clean whole view binds the spoken name to the object before a chain of details or styling examples. This is not permission to introduce the target early in a delayed-reveal concept.
Feature: show the specific visible reason to want it
New close compositions of the actual named material, edge, hardware or handle action; maintain garment/person continuity if tied to one look.
Enter on the feature phrase. Exit after that feature is inspectable and before the script resumes a whole-outfit consequence. Return to a relevant whole look, not automatically a full-screen face.
Proposed 1.5–4s per distinct feature; longer if action requires. Direct cuts; no decorative macro morph.
The close view supplies visible support for the specific descriptor. Unsupported interior, capacity or construction demonstrations remain asset/evidence gaps.
Styling demonstration: connect details to a complete look
A distinct full or three-quarter outfit with the product visibly carried; for a multi-look guide use different subjects/settings where required, then a matching accessory detail if spoken.
Enter on the outfit, city or use-context cue. A detail insert starts at its exact phrase and rejoins the complete look or next distinct example. Keep the guide continuous.
Proposed 3–7s per useful look; longer approved descriptions can use a separate relevant angle/action. Finish a pickup, turn or carry before leaving it.
The viewer sees what the product does for an outfit. Named locations organize examples; unrelated skyline B-roll would hide the styling the speaker is explaining.
Synthesis or reassurance: explain the common principle
Stable guide over a fresh quiet wardrobe/product composition, leaving room for a meaningful expression or single pointing gesture.
Enter when the guide interprets the examples; hold across the connected thought. Leave on the concrete future-use moment. Full-screen presenter is optional only if deliberately planned.
Proposed 2–4s or the actual interpretive phrase. Direct background reset; no forced punch-in or hand-wave transition.
The guide links the distinct examples into a usable decision. A calm background prevents new visual information from competing with the summary; fresh arrangement avoids replaying prior B-roll.
Future pacing: show the desired life moment
A new location and action: arriving at lunch, adjusting a coat at a train door, or joining an occasion while wearing the styled product.
Enter on the exact imagined-use or supported experience phrase. Hold long enough to understand the setting and complete the action; exit on the actual invitation.
Proposed 3–5s, adjusted to action/voice. Direct cut, no mandatory dreamy dissolve or slow motion.
A specific event lets the viewer imagine enjoying the look. Label hypothetical scenes as such in the plan; synthetic people and reactions are not customer proof.
Actual current product page with readable identity and terms, or a fresh accurate product composition plus one valid action.
Enter during the spoken action/destination. Hide or reposition the guide only to expose essential page content; the voice continues. Hold the result of any real scroll.
Proposed 3–6s including spoken CTA, with a trial 0.2–0.8s after the last word if already readable. Extend for actual reading need. Direct cut/end; no invented sale UI.
The viewer connects the item to the next action. Showing the destination during speech reduces unnecessary silent ending time while preserving comprehension.
styles: G-PRES

One consistent original/authorized creator, conversational expression and ordinary gesture, clean keyed silhouette without a rectangle. Generate still anchor with GPT Image 2 and use the currently authorized speaking-video route.
Persistent orientation layer through the story; a fresh subdued background can support interpretation. Move/hide only for a documented composition need.
G-HOOK

Immediately desirable carry/action or an optional grid of distinct actual approved style sources. Natural or candid photographic conditions as the selected mode requires; preserve subject/product provenance.
Opening only when it serves the spoken proposition. Grid count and designer-bag use are brief-specific; neither implies endorsement, ownership or real customers.
G-LOOK

Full-length or useful three-quarter outfit, visible bag/shoes, ordinary daylight, plausible mirror/friend/propped-phone framing or restrained natural fashion direction. One readable step, turn or adjustment.
Styling examples and recognizable wardrobe tension. Phone-like appearance does not prove phone capture; generated scenes stay labeled as illustrations.
G-DETAIL
Distinct actual material, edge, hardware or matching-jewelry views; appropriate viewing scale, natural surface response and source-supported geometry. Still holds are valid.
Exact feature/selection phrases. A model-specific insert retains the same sleeve, hand context and setting; a crop does not count as new B-roll.
G-PRODUCT
Unobstructed selected product/color from approved references, natural chair/table/window context or clean product view, optional supported hand touch.
Named introduction and object recognition; can close if the actual CTA needs no page. Do not silently substitute a different revision or show unverified hidden construction.
G-RECAP
Face-free wardrobe arrangement, real dressing objects, product plus complementary clothing; fresh framing and natural light.
Category consideration or synthesis after examples. The wardrobe relation conveys the principle without replaying the montage.
G-LIFE
Distinct aspirational context with a meaningful action and readable styling; plausible human behavior, same selected product identity, ordinary surroundings appropriate to the brand.
Future pacing or a genuinely supported experience. Generated acted use is not testimony, documentary evidence or measured before/after.
G-PAGE
Authentic current destination capture, legible product name/photo and relevant terms; controlled real scroll if helpful. Alternative: G-PRODUCT with a separate truthful action label.
Closing decision and next step. Stop movement for reading; free the key controls from guide/captions. Refresh volatile page/offer facts before production.
concepts.assets: One guide identity/reference and separate clean presenter source; exact approved narration and provider voice selection; distinct hook and every covering scene/insert; first-frame image for each planned motion scene; selected product/color/revision references; current destination capture or truthful closing composition; separate caption/CTA layers; source/generation provenance; a single final alignment and optional keep/remove map. When storyboarding is requested, attach all selected first assets to the correct Cut Room cards and preserve separate reference evidence.
concepts.calibration: W01 combines an earlier Nuamore 24.600s reference audit, Eleanor travel production history and Vivienne’s corrected 35.9167s picture export. This update directly inspected three retained Nuamore boundary sheets, an Eleanor overview and 40 exact decoded Vivienne frames on three sheets, including all nine base-cut pairs. It does not claim a new exhaustive review of those videos or direct audio audition. Vivienne boundaries begin at frames 77, 141, 220, 330, 408, 454, 548, 648 and 746 (24fps); the guide moves right at 548 and is absent from the PDP at 746. Eleanor’s prior audit records longer city holds, a background step crop, and 28 matched presenter/voice intervals after quiet-gap removal. Actual source-project settings are history, not presets for a new asset.
concepts.evidence_boundary: The workspace audit distinguishes retained-frame observations, prior production receipts, explicit dated user corrections and proposed adaptation. This turn did not repeat full-motion review or directly audition audio. Recorded source settings apply only to those source projects; their performance and product-claim applicability are not established by this profile. All adjustable target windows below remain proposals.

edit.coverage: Use a full-frame background track plus one independent keyed guide, exact phrase captions, optional specific label/CTA and continuous narration. The background is often the principal visual evidence, not a generic insert covering a talking-head scene. Keep the guide’s identity/wardrobe stable; independent fashion examples may intentionally feature different people. Lock separate visual and spoken product-reveal cues. A no-guide destination ending is allowed when the selected mode needs legibility.
edit.cuts: Cut the background on a new idea, item, feature scale, useful action completion or destination cue. Keep expressive guide delivery continuous across picture changes. Protect product recognition, full-outfit inspection, matching-detail comprehension and the completed pickup/turn. Do not cut on every caption phrase. Quiet-gap joins inside one background scene are not new scenes. Inspect adjoining source/target frames for every meaningful boundary; use actual aligned speech rather than estimating a cut from a script word count.
edit.transitions: Direct background cuts are the baseline established by these examples. The presenter and captions do not dissolve with the background. A planned background-only detail step crop is a framing event. Do not add whooshes, whip pans, flashes, morphs or dissolves at every clause. If another reference warrants a transition, name its affected layers, cue, handles and reason. Layout changes happen at a meaning/scene boundary with a clear subject to uncover; avoid arbitrary presenter travel.
edit.broll: Choose the next background by what the line makes inspectable: complete look for styling, distinct material/detail for a descriptor, matching accessory for a relationship, fresh everyday scene for imagined use, real destination for action. Give every insert a start cue, finish cue and return/next-view decision. Same presenter is intentional continuity; repeated backgrounds, recolors, mirrors and crops are not independent variety. Keep stills as stills where useful. Use the defined mode’s coherent treatment across the entire ad instead of making every section polished commercial footage or every hook distressed phone footage.
edit.motion: Separate genuine captured/generated subject action from post transforms. A step, cuff adjustment, bag lift or chair pull supplies useful motion; allow its result to appear. Use a restrained background step crop only when the next phrase names a smaller detail and resolution supports it. Keep the guide and captions fixed during that crop. Do not animate every still or repeat a short action loop to fill narration. Presenter size must be assessed from visible silhouette at the actual aspect ratio; trial roughly 25–35% picture height, then adjust to product/face/hand clearance. Exact source pan/tilt/zoom values are not transferable.
edit.text: Align exact approved captions to the selected final voice. Use readable short semantic groups, with natural line breaks and sufficient contrast; approximately 3–6 words can be a trial, not a segmentation law. Negation must remain understandable across phrase changes. Protect face, hands, key product details, full-look shoes and current platform UI. Keep captions, city/item labels and CTA as separate events. The source white sans-serif/outline treatment can guide a target, but no exact font/size match is inferred from thumbnails. Refresh page/price/stock text from actual evidence.
edit.audio: Select the exact requested provider voice before avatar production. The historical Woman Over 40 choice meant the named ElevenLabs voice, not an age prompt. Keep identity/settings/source hash recorded; no automatic cloning. Use current authorized presenter route; HeyGen in W01 was explicitly requested for those projects and is not a blanket exception to Google Omni. Prefer finalized, conservatively tightened narration before a new audio-driven avatar when supported. For existing matched audio/video, apply the same ordered keep/remove map and re-align captions, background cues and CTA. Preserve words, pronunciation and selected speed; do not double-apply 1.1×. Mute unwanted generated B-roll audio; select no music or a licensed low bed deliberately. Review actual lip sync and intelligibility, disclosing if audio QA is only model-assisted.
edit.finish: Keep coherent natural skin/material color and a clean keyed edge on both light and dark plates. Match backgrounds to the chosen phone-like or natural-fashion treatment without adding shake/grain as authenticity proof. No forced slow motion, beauty filter or perpetual smile. Distinct scene actions and product construction must survive source-to-export review. Respect source duration at differing fps; converting frame cadence must not retime voice. Preserve native provider files, selected revisions and original exports. A static guide or unverified render is a work in progress.
edit.ending: Enter the ending while the invitation is spoken. Use either a real current page or an accurate product-plus-action composition; no mandatory discount or scarcity. Clear the guide if she covers relevant page content, as in Vivienne; retain her if the product/action are readable, as in Eleanor. A short 0.2–0.8s post-speech hold is a proposed trial, not a source-wide rule. Extend for comprehension, not padding. Resolve the reveal policy from the brief; old-money target delay does not override a product-visible Vivienne-style hook.
edit.adapt: At short duration use fewer distinct arguments/examples and lighter caption load within authorized copy scope; preserve exact locked words. At longer duration add genuinely different styled examples, actions or relevant evidence, not replayed photos or stretched short clips. Long city descriptions can hold a meaningful look or introduce a distinct feature view at its exact cue. Do not force the 24.6s Nuamore runtime, the 70.667s Eleanor timing or the 35.9167s Vivienne picture length onto a new script. Preserve product/reveal constraints when changing mode. Surface duration conflicts instead of silently speeding speech.
edit.reject: Reject wrong library voice, a generic maturity substitute, unsupported provider exceptions, a static guide described as speaking, independent audio/presenter cuts, captions left on the pre-trim timeline, arbitrary side switching, guide/product overlap, unreadable grids/PDP, repeated inserts disguised as crops, unsupported product details, invented customer proof and expired offer claims. Inspect the selected first frames and finished export; verify all source/target joins, matte, full product visibility, whole-ad variety and exact ending. Model QA can miss a corner shift; source frames and actual receipts resolve contradictions. No performance claim follows from creative resemblance.
